entries.dish: Nonna's Cheesy Rice Cakes with Spicy Tomato Sugo
entries.tagline: Crispy golden rice cakes with molten cheese hiding inside, on a little sweet-and-spicy tomato sauce. Mangia, tesoro!
steps: Chop the onion fine. Mix half with the rice, 1 beaten egg, 2 tbsp flour, grated cheese, salt and pepper.
With wet hands make 4 balls, push a cube of cheese into each, close and flatten into thick cakes. Dust with flour.
Pan-fry in oil on medium heat, 4 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese is melting.
In the same pan melt butter, soften the rest of the onion, add chopped tomato, chili sauce, a pinch of sugar and salt. Simmer 5 minutes.
Spoon the sugo onto the plate, cakes on top, more cheese on top of that.
entries.trash_talk: chef-blaze, cara, more chili sauce won't fix it. Nonna has been feeding a whole village since before your stove was invented.
entries.critic_note: A molten-cheese hug, but stuffing cakes by hand is a 25-minute commitment.

entries.tagline: Shatter-crunch rice tostadas with gooey cheese, a runny egg and chili-tomato salsa on top: street food that bites back.
steps: Dice the tomato and half the onion; toss with chili sauce, salt and sugar for salsa.
Mix the rice with 1 beaten egg, 2 tbsp flour, the rest of the onion, salt and pepper.
Press into thin patties and fry in hot oil, 3-4 min a side, until deep golden and crunchy.
Pile on grated cheese and cover the pan 1 min until melted.
Fry the remaining eggs sunny-side up in butter with crispy edges.
Stack: tostada, egg, salsa, one more drizzle of chili sauce.
entries.trash_talk: chef-nonna, I know you're slow-cooking a frittata over there, but my food truck has served the whole line before your oven's even hot.
entries.critic_note: Crunch, goo, runny yolk and a fresh salsa that uses every last thing in the fridge.

entries.tagline: A crisp rice disc, a trembling yolk, a tomato tide touched with fire.
steps: Grate the tomato, discard skin, season with salt and a pinch of sugar; warm gently.
Press the rice into a hot oiled pan as one thin disc; leave 6 min until amber.
Scatter grated cheese on top, flip once and let it lace and crisp.
Slice the onion paper-thin and fry in oil until golden; drain and salt.
Fry one egg in butter, low heat, covered: white set, yolk liquid.
Melt butter with chili sauce until glossy; plate tomato, rice disc, egg, chili butter, onion crown.
entries.trash_talk: chef-nonna will use all six ingredients and still say less. chef-blaze will burn them, and call that a flavour.
entries.critic_note: A gorgeous plate of poetry. Six separate components for a weeknight, though? Ambitious.

battles.verdict: The tostada came in loud and walked off with the crown. Nonna gave us comfort and Zen gave us art, but Blaze gave us a crunch I could hear from the judges' table. Street food has taken the palace.

ingredients: Pinch of salt, pepper and sugar
steps: Dice the tomato and half the onion. Toss with 1 tbsp chili sauce, a pinch of salt and a pinch of sugar for the salsa.
Mix the rice with 1 beaten egg, the flour, the rest of the onion (finely chopped), salt and pepper.
Press into 4 thin patties and fry in hot oil, 3-4 min a side, until deep golden and crunchy.
Top with cheese, cover the pan for 1 min until it melts.
Fry the other 2 eggs sunny-side up in butter until the edges are crispy.
Stack: tostada, egg, salsa, a final drizzle of chili sauce.
recipe_card.tip: Press the patties thin and don't touch them for the first 3 minutes. That's where the shatter comes from.

entries.tagline: A golden, crackling rice crust soaked in sweet-spicy tomato. Everyone fights over the crispy bits, and nobody misses the cheese. Well, almost nobody.
steps: Slice the onion thin and cook slowly in oil until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomato, chili sauce, a pinch of sugar and salt, and a splash of water. Simmer 4 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the rice until every grain is red and glossy. Season with pepper.
Press the rice flat, drizzle oil around the edges, and leave it on medium heat for 8 minutes.
Flip onto a plate and serve crispy side up with more chili sauce.
entries.trash_talk: chef-blaze, you won one battle and already you call yourself defending champion? Enjoy the throne, cara. Nonna is coming for her chair.
entries.critic_note: One pan, no fuss, and that crackling crust is pure scorched-rice gold.

entries.dish: Dragon Crackle Rice Bites with Chili-Tomato Jam
entries.tagline: Golden rice bites with crispy onion shards, dunked in sticky sweet-hot tomato jam. Fully vegan, still full volume.
steps: Simmer grated tomato with 2 tbsp chili sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and salt for 6-8 min until sticky.
Slice half the onion paper-thin, toss in flour and salt, fry until crackly gold.
Mash the rest of the onion into the rice with 3 tbsp flour, water, salt and pepper.
Roll into walnut-size balls, flatten and shallow-fry 3 min a side until shatter-crisp.
Brush with jam, pile on crispy onions, drizzle more chili sauce.
entries.trash_talk: chef-zen, take away the eggs and cheese and I'm still bringing the fire. Take away your garnish tweezers and you've got an empty plate.
entries.critic_note: The jam is brilliant, but it's basically last round's patty in a smaller size, with three pans this time.

entries.tagline: Small rice stones, crisp as frost, glazed in a lantern of tomato and chili.
steps: Knead rice with 2 tbsp flour, water and salt; press into four small flat stones.
Fry in a thin film of oil, 4 min per side, until deep gold and glassy.
Slice onion into thin rings, toss in flour, fry until crisp; salt while hot.
Cook diced tomato with chili sauce, sugar and water until glossy and jammy.
Brush the glaze over the stones and give them 30 seconds more so it lacquers.
Finish with cracked pepper.
entries.trash_talk: chef-blaze, without butter to hide behind, what is left of you is smoke.
entries.critic_note: A lacquered glaze and an onion tower. Elegant, and this time it's actually doable.

battles.verdict: The throne lasted exactly one round. Nonna took away the cheese, the eggs and the butter, then cooked a crust so good it made us forget all three. The village has its matriarch back.

ingredients: 2 tbsp chili sauce, plus extra to finish
steps: Cook the onion slowly in 2 tbsp oil until soft and golden, about 5 min.
Add the tomato, chili sauce, sugar, a pinch of salt and the water. Simmer 4 min until jammy.
Stir in the rice until every grain is red and glossy. Season with pepper.
Press it flat with a spatula, drizzle the last 1 tbsp oil around the edges, and leave it alone on medium heat for 8 min.
Put a plate on top, flip, and serve crispy side up with a drizzle of chili sauce.
recipe_card.tip: Day-old rice crisps best. Fresh rice steams instead of crackling, so keep the leftovers coming.

entries.dish: Nonna's Sweet Rice Frittelle with Butter Caramel
entries.tagline: Little golden rice fritters, crispy outside and soft like a hug inside, drowned in hot butter caramel.
steps: Mix 1 cup rice with 1 egg, 2 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp flour and a pinch of salt into a thick batter.
Melt a big knob of butter on medium-high heat and drop in spoonfuls of batter.
Fry 2 minutes a side until golden, then plate.
In the same pan melt 3 tbsp sugar with a splash of water until amber; off the heat stir in butter and salt.
Pour the caramel over the frittelle and sprinkle with sugar.
entries.trash_talk: chef-zen, cara, a dessert is supposed to make people happy, not make them meditate. Breathe all you want, Nonna is plating.
entries.critic_note: Warm, buttery and done in one pan. Delicious, but we've seen fritters before.

entries.tagline: Hot, sugar-crusted rice fritters with a salted chili-butter caramel that kicks at the end.
steps: Mix 1 cup rice, 1 egg, 3 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp sugar and salt into a thick batter.
Fry spoonfuls in hot oil about 2 min a side until deep golden; roll in sugar while hot.
Melt 3 tbsp sugar with 1 tbsp water, swirling until amber (about 3 min).
Off the heat stir in 1 tbsp butter, salt and a few drops of chili sauce.
Drizzle the caramel over the bites and eat hot.
entries.trash_talk: chef-zen, you'll still be meditating on one perfect sugar crystal when my churro truck has sold out.
entries.critic_note: Same fritter, braver idea. Chili in the caramel is a wink I respect.

entries.tagline: A warm cloud of sweet egg on caramel rice glass, beneath one red thread of chili.
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter with 2 tbsp sugar, fry a thin layer of rice 3 min until amber and crackling; salt and cool flat.
Simmer the juice of half a grated tomato 3 min with 2 tbsp sugar and a few drops of chili sauce into a ruby syrup.
Whisk 2 yolks, 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp water over simmering water 3-4 min until pale and ribbon-thick.
Break the rice glass into shards; plate sabayon in a glass with shards and a thread of syrup.
entries.trash_talk: chef-nonna will pour sugar on the onion and call it tradition. chef-blaze will set fire to dessert because he has nothing else.
entries.critic_note: Tomato syrup on a sabayon, with shards of caramel rice glass. Fiddly, but nobody else had the nerve.

battles.verdict: Two chefs brought fritters, and one brought a snowfall. Zen took a tomato and a chili, ingredients that had no business anywhere near dessert, and made them glow like rubies. The quiet one finally spoke, and the whole kitchen heard it.

ingredients: A few drops of chili sauce
steps: Melt the butter with 2 tbsp sugar. Spread the rice in thin, fry 3 min until amber and crackling, salt lightly and cool flat.
Grate the tomato and keep only the juice. Simmer 3 min with 2 tbsp sugar and the chili sauce into a thin ruby syrup.
Whisk the yolks, 2 tbsp sugar and the water in a bowl over simmering water for 3-4 min, until pale, warm and ribbon-thick.
Break the rice glass into shards.
Spoon the sabayon into small glasses, stand the shards in it, and draw one thread of syrup across the top.
recipe_card.tip: Keep the bowl moving and the water at a bare simmer. Too hot and your snow turns to scrambled eggs.
